video_title: What Happens When AI Agents Can Spend Your Money?
gist: a16z's Alex Rampell and VGS chief strategy officer Terry Angelos discuss how payment credentials turn AI agents into actors, the wallet wars, the shift from walled-garden to network agentic tokens (VGS now issues a few million per week), and open liability and merchant-access questions.

insights.claim: In roughly the last three months AI agents moved from spectators that recommend purchases to actors that complete them, because payment credentials give them 'arms and legs'; this sharply raises agent utility.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce is shifting from demo to real transaction volume; watch credential-handling infrastructure.
insights.quote: agents being what I would call spectators to agents being actors

insights.claim: A concrete agent task (finding, scheduling and booking a piano teacher around soccer days) was done end-to-end in one session, versus a prior ChatGPT session that only gave recommendations.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Shows consumer-grade completion of multi-step transactions is already working.

insights.claim: Agentic-commerce demand is partly unmonetized: an always-on agent in a group chat could buy items on every recommendation (e.g. cycling tires), implying incremental consumer spend rather than only substitution.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Upside to GDP/merchant sales from latent demand; agents may also cut spend by cancelling forgotten subscriptions.

insights.claim: Wallets are racing to connect to agents; an agent wants the wallet with the most consumers holding credentials and the broadest merchant reach. Cited scale: Stripe Link ~300M consumers and ~1M merchants, Shopify Shop Pay ~1.7M merchants, PayPal 400M+ accounts and ~30M merchants.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Distribution (consumer accounts x merchant reach) determines which wallets win agent default status.
insights.quote: wallet wars where every wallet is now rushing to connect to the agents

insights.claim: Being the default or top-of-wallet credential has long been valuable: issuers paid tens of millions of dollars to Uber and Airbnb to prefer their cards, so the same fight will recur for default credentials inside agent flows.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Expect issuers and networks to pay or compete for default status in agent wallets.

insights.claim: Wallets come in two forms: those that merely hold and hand over a tokenized credential (Apple Pay) and those that transact and remit to the merchant (Shop Pay, Link, PayPal); agentic commerce blends the two.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Helps classify who captures economics and liability in agent checkout.

insights.claim: Stripe's Link-in-agent flow is an AOL-style walled garden: when Link had no Walmart connection, Stripe issued a one-time Visa virtual card to buy and then charged the user in a second transaction.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Works but breaks merchant relationship, upsell and dispute handling.
insights.quote: Stripe in many ways is like the AOL of agentic commerce

insights.claim: The virtual-card workaround breaks chargebacks and merchant follow-on sales: the bank sees a Stripe transaction not Walmart, a test user's Amex dispute routed to a Stripe engineer's cell phone, and a Walmart Plus offer failed because the one-time card was dead.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Merchants and issuers need the user's real card in the flow; the intermediated model is unscalable.

insights.claim: Card networks have released 'agentic tokens', a new 16-digit number that lets a wallet safely hand a credential to a verified agent with a spend limit, so the merchant charges the user's own card and chargebacks plus follow-on selling are preserved.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Open network standards are the direction of travel and entrench card-network rails in agentic commerce.

insights.claim: VGS says it is the largest provisioner of agentic tokens, for agents, wallets and some merchants; volume went from zero three months earlier to a few million tokens per week.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Hard adoption datapoint for an early agentic-commerce infrastructure ramp (company-reported, board-insider).
insights.quote: this was you know zero three months ago. Now we're doing a few million of these tokens per week

insights.claim: Chargebacks and card-network dispute rules are a key trust mechanism and the reason card rails beat bearer instruments like crypto for agent purchases.
insights.speaker: Alex Rampell
insights.so_what: Argues against crypto-native agent payments for consumer goods where recourse matters.
insights.quote: it's a bearer instrument. I pay with crypto, I'm never getting that back.

insights.claim: VGS secures credentials for about a third of all e-commerce by GMV and holds roughly 10 billion credentials, serving the largest online merchants, neobanks and frontier AI labs.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Scale and neutrality make VGS a chokepoint for credential handoff to agents.

insights.claim: Merchants above $1B GMV typically run three to five payment processors, and a neutral vault avoids storing and updating hundreds of millions of cards separately at each processor.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Multi-processor merchants structurally need independent vaulting, supporting VGS demand.

insights.claim: About a third of cards turn over each year (about 25% from 4-year expiry plus about 5% from events like Capital One buying Discover or fraud), so card-update tooling is a recurring need.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Credential refresh is a durable revenue driver independent of agents.

insights.claim: Vaults are moving from single-player (store for one's own subscription) to multiplayer (credentials shared with processors, wallets and agents under open standards), which makes the vault business more valuable.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Network-effect brokerage of credentials is the core of the VGS bull case.
insights.quote: vaults are going from single player to multiplayer

insights.claim: VGS describes three overlapping eras: the trusted vault (about 10 years), the flow of updates and network tokens in and out of it, and a 'network' era brokering credentials among parties including agentic commerce and bank tokenization.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Company strategy: layer services on the vault to compound network effects.

insights.claim: VGS takes merchants and AI companies out of PCI DSS scope, which is required by every bank to process or issue cards, so AI apps can transact without holding card data.
insights.speaker: Alex Rampell
insights.so_what: Compliance burden makes outsourcing credential handling attractive for AI firms.

themes.theme: Liability and trust for agent purchases

insights.claim: Agent transactions raise three checks: is the card real, is the requester the valid owner (agents must be registered with Visa, Mastercard or Amex and pass context such as amount), and is the agent of sound mind; the third, hallucination or error liability, is unresolved.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Dispute and liability rules for agent mistakes are the open gap; agents will probably have to take on some responsibility.
insights.quote: is the agent of sound mind?

insights.claim: Delegated authority could become a competitive feature: agent providers may offer to absorb liability for erroneous purchases to win users, because merchants will not accept 'my agent got it wrong' and friendly-fraud risk could grow.
insights.speaker: Alex Rampell
insights.so_what: Possible new insurance or guarantee products around agents.

insights.claim: Amazon recently blocked a major consumer agent mainly because its advertising model monetizes shopper eyeballs, which agents lack; blocking is rational for ad-driven retailers and not simply Luddism.
insights.speaker: Alex Rampell
insights.so_what: Ad-funded marketplaces are the likeliest to resist agents; receptive merchants may capture agent traffic.
insights.quote: Amazon is an advertising company and they want you and your eyeballs going to their website.

insights.claim: Merchant postures will split: Amazon fears, Walmart may welcome agents given inventory and last-mile delivery, and Shopify's small merchants likely see agents as a vital new channel; merchants may also deploy their own sales agents.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Watch Walmart and Shopify merchants as early winners; Amazon as holdout.

insights.claim: Open banking offers a template: banks like Chase forced aggregators like Plaid onto tokenized, limited, sometimes paid APIs after a negotiated settlement, so merchants may similarly demand sanctioned APIs for agent access.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Expect negotiated, possibly fee-bearing agent access rather than pure scraping or logins.

insights.claim: Early consumer wins from agents rest on asymmetry (few have the tool, counterparties don't notice) and will erode as the other side adapts, e.g. companies blocking agent logins or demanding the human.
insights.speaker: Alex Rampell
insights.so_what: Agent arbitrage gains are transient; do not extrapolate early consumer savings.

insights.claim: Overhyped: agents will not trigger deposit runs by chasing yield, because friction such as bill-pay integrations keeps balances in primary banks like Chase even when Mercury pays more.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Lowers risk of agent-driven deposit flight for incumbent banks.

insights.claim: Card rewards programs with breakage could unravel if agents route each purchase to the card with the best points, hitting the issuer economics behind rewards.
insights.speaker: Terry Angelos (VGS)
insights.so_what: Negative for breakage-dependent rewards economics; watch for revised terms and conditions.
insights.quote: the whole points reward ecosystem falls apart
